criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines name the mechanism (Enhanced Use Lease solicitation), the news trigger (June 5 posting, June 29 deadline), and the stake (4,700 acres, three Alaska bases). 'For the first time, commercial AI compute could occupy federal military land in Alaska' signals the structural tension without snark. Minor dock: 'could occupy' softens the correction signal slightly.

criteria.name: Mechanism load-bearing + AK consequence
criteria.notes: 10 USC 2667 EUL is Alaska's only active federal pathway for private AI compute on publicly controlled land in 2026. Consequence names sector (AI/defense-tech infrastructure), decision risk (2028 gas cliff, 24-month build window), named actors (Chugach Electric, GVEA, AFCEC, ANC firms), and hard timeframe (June 29 deadline, Q3 2026 award). All four elements present and specific.

criteria.name: Layer fidelity
criteria.notes: All five dossier layers are present in the bullet block. Controlling actors match exactly: Office of the President/SAF/IE, Robert Moriarty by name, AFCEC/CI Installations Directorate, Chugach Electric Association (JBER)/GVEA (Eielson/Clear SFS), RFLP respondent. No invented layers or actors. Chain is complete and readable.

criteria.name: Chokepoint clarity
criteria.notes: One layer (AFCEC/CI Solicitation Gate), one actor (AFCEC/CI), one binary (accept or reject proposals by June 29). 'No federal appeal path for developers if AFCEC issues a no-award determination' names the asymmetry precisely. Matches dossier chokepoint on all three dimensions.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: 'The utility layer, not the military layer, is the real constraint' is a specific, debatable position. The EUL-durability-vs-appropriations argument adds a second structural claim. Minor dock: thesis is distributed across two paragraphs rather than a single sharp sentence.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names the concrete action (written utility indication-of-interest before June 29), who needs to act (developers evaluating EUL bids), what failure looks like (proposal fails at utility layer even after AFCEC award), the binary outcome by Q3 2026, and the 2028 gas cliff as the separating variable.

criteria.name: Primary-source quality
criteria.notes: Dossier confirms all five layers carry verified primary sources: House.gov for 10 USC 2667 (statute), Air and Space Forces Magazine for SAF/IE layer, ADN for utility constraints (primary reporting), KTUU for news trigger. Minor dock: EO layer's primary source routes through globalsecurity.org rather than federalregister.gov directly.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, position-taking throughout. Statutory citation (10 USC 2667), named actors, specific dates, and the square-bracket layer device are all on-brand. No banned phrases, no LinkedIn-influencer drift, no explainer-bot hedging. Minor dock: 'forcing function' is mildly tech-jargon but analytically precise.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Word count approximately 448, within the 350-475 window. Total character count 2,989, under 3000. Paragraphs are 1-3 sentences. Bullet block has 5 items (upper bound of 3-5). Minor dock: utility layer bullet runs multi-clause at 37 words.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: 'Should AFCEC treat a utility indication-of-interest as a mandatory proposal element, or does requiring it risk excluding developers best positioned to solve the power problem independently?' Real, debatable, tied directly to the chokepoint and the structural tension. No CTA, no follow prompt.

one_sentence_fix: Replace 'could occupy' in the third hook sentence with a declarative statement — e.g., 'For the first time, private AI compute would sit on federal military land in Alaska' — to sharpen the correction signal without hedging.
